title: The Late Homework
moral: Truthfulness is not only about telling facts. It is also about being fair, kind, and brave when a mistake happens.

pages.text:
Meera liked finishing homework early.

She sharpened her pencils, wrote the date neatly, and kept her books in order. Her brother called her Homework Minister.

One Tuesday, Miss Roy gave the class a worksheet.

"Bring it tomorrow," she said. "No excuses."

Meera placed it carefully in her folder.

After school, her friend Sana came home with her.

They worked together at the dining table. Sana finished first and packed her bag quickly because her mother was waiting downstairs.

The next morning, Miss Roy asked everyone to take out the worksheet.

Meera opened her folder.

It was not there.

She searched her bag. English book. Maths book. Tiffin box. One old wrapper. No worksheet.

Her heart jumped.

Then Sana turned around from the front row. Her face looked worried.

"I think I took yours by mistake," Sana whispered. "I have two."

Meera stared at her.

Miss Roy was coming closer.

Sana's eyes filled with fear. "Please don't tell. She will scold me."

Meera felt stuck. If she said nothing, Miss Roy would think Meera had forgotten. If she told the truth, Sana might get in trouble.

Miss Roy reached her desk.

"Meera, your worksheet?"

Meera stood slowly.

"Ma'am, Sana took mine by mistake yesterday. She did not mean to. I also should have checked my folder before she left."

Sana looked down.

Miss Roy paused. "Thank you for telling me clearly."

She took one worksheet from Sana and gave it to Meera.

"No scolding today," Miss Roy said. "But both of you must check your bags next time."

Sana breathed out so loudly that Rohan whispered, "A balloon has survived."

Meera almost laughed.

At lunch, Sana sat beside her.

"You could have blamed me," Sana said.

Meera shook her head. "It was a mistake. Mistakes need fixing, not hiding."

Sana smiled and gave her half a sandwich. It was cucumber, not Meera's favourite. But that day it tasted like friendship.
